human_tolerance.notes: Roosts in cracks and crevices, including tile roofs, exfoliating bark and rock outcrops, so it readily occupies buildings; open porches are used as night roosts. Forages low over the ground, 1-2 m up, and will hunt around outside lights. Sensitive to anthropogenic noise, which can cut foraging efficiency severalfold.

phases.name: mating
phases.note: Mating season October to February, taken while the bats are in hibernation; males store sperm in spring and summer, females store it until they emerge in spring.

phases.name: dormancy
phases.note: Shallow bouts of torpor through the cold months, in buildings, caves and cracks in rock. Overlaps the mating phase on purpose: copulation happens during hibernation.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Females emerge from hibernation in spring, come into estrus, and give birth to one or two pups in early June.

phases.name: young
phases.note: Pups make short flights at four to five weeks and are weaned at 40 to 45 days, so they are on the wing from early July and flying well by August.

vocalizations.description: A rapid train of very high-frequency clicks, produced in the larynx and usually through the open mouth, used in flight and on approach to the roost.
A harsh, grating shriek exchanged between roosting individuals and between a mother and young, given at close range.

range.note: Wikipedia gives the range as western Canada to central Mexico and describes the species as typical of arid and semi-arid, often mountainous and rocky, habitat. The country list is that range expressed as ISO 3166-1 codes; the Koppen list is the climate classes of that range, taken from Wikipedia's biome categories rather than measured per-country.

traits.mass_kg.note: 14-25 g from Wikipedia; mass_kg is the midpoint, 19.5 g.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: The 14-25 g range from Wikipedia, converted to kilograms.

traits.length_m.note: length_m is the head-and-body length of 6.2-7.9 cm from Wikipedia, taking 7 cm, and excludes the 3.9-4.9 cm tail, as the field is body length rather than total length here.

traits.wingspan_m.note: 15-16 inches (38-40 cm) from Wikipedia, taken as 39 cm.

traits.lifespan_y.note: No longevity figure appears in the cited sources. 12 years is an informed estimate for a large-bodied vespertilionid bat and is a placeholder, not a measurement: replace it if a sourced figure for this species is found.

traits.diet.note: Wikipedia describes an insectivore taking crickets and other arthropods, able to eat up to half its weight in insects a night, with facultative nectar-feeding from columnar cacti in spring and cactus fruit in summer. Shares weight that mostly insect, small nectar, small fruit.

traits.social.note: Wikipedia describes colonies roosting in crevices and in buildings, with a night roost nearer the foraging ground. A colony can hold many individuals, so group_size is given a wide 1-200 span; the roost is crevice-based rather than a fixed cave colony.

traits.senses.note: Wikipedia notes the bats echolocate in flight but often do not echolocate while foraging and instead locate insects on the ground with their large ears, relying on the prey's own sounds, which is the basis for high hearing.

traits.wariness.note: Authored judgement: roosts in buildings and tolerates disturbance, but flees readily and avoids well-lit ground, so wariness sits mid-range.

traits.defense.note: Flees rather than fighting: Wikipedia lists snakes, cats, foxes, coyotes and raccoons as terrestrial predators of the bats while they feed on the ground, and crepuscular and nocturnal raptors as the main predator of adults and young.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Powered flight from Wikipedia; climbing is included because bats haul themselves up into cracks and hang from their hind limbs and thumbs, which is how the record reaches a crevice roost.

traits.nest_type.note: Roosts in cracks and crevices, tile roofs, under exfoliating bark and in rock outcrops, which is cavity nesting rather than a built nest.

traits.perching.note: Roosts by hanging from the hind limbs, so a perched state is needed. The biped_winged plan's built-in perched animation is an upright cling with the wings folded, not an inverted hang, because the kit has no inverted pose; the record therefore shows the bat folded up on a roost face rather than hanging head-down. The behaviour programme keeps it at the roost by day, so the scene reads as roosting rather than as an upside-down bat.

traits.size_class.note: From mass_kg: 19.5 g is Tiny (< 0.05 kg).

habitat.use.note: Foraging flight dominates: Wikipedia says the bats fly low, 1-2 m off the ground, gleaning prey from the surface, with some time in trees and rock crevices.

habitat.resources.note: Weighted from the diet shares, with the crevice roost carrying the shelter weight.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Wikipedia records tile roofs and buildings as day roosts and open porches as night roosts, and reports that traffic noise reduces foraging efficiency by up to threefold, so the species adapts to suburbs but avoids noisy, brightly lit ground.

seasonal.strategy.note: Wikipedia describes winter torpor in buildings, caves and rock cracks, and mating during that period.

seasonal.triggers.note: Authored, not measured. Wikipedia states the species takes shallow bouts of torpor in winter and that mating occurs during hibernation, but gives no temperature threshold. 5 C is an authored cut-off for a desert bat's winter nights and stands in until a sourced figure exists; the dormancy phase is the part that is actually sourced.

seasonal.phases.note: Mating October to February during torpor, birth of one or two pups in early June, and night foraging outside the coldest months, all from Wikipedia.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Wikipedia: pups are 3-3.5 g at birth, make short flights at four to five weeks, are weaned at 40-45 days and reach adult size at about eight weeks. The record carries no egg stage, because a bat gives birth to live young; the schema's first listed stage is retained as Egg and read as the pre-birth stage.

vocalizations.echolocation_click.note: Wikipedia states the species echolocates while foraging and travelling, using laryngeal clicks, and may stop echolocating while gleaning.

vocalizations.social_call.note: Authored: bats roosting in tight crevices call to one another at close range, and the record's Colony social structure implies it. Wikipedia does not describe the call itself.

look.note: Colours follow Wikipedia: fur pale at the roots and brown on the back with a light underside, long forward-pointing ears over 2.5 cm, and a blunt piglike snout. The kit has no bat mesh, so the model uses the biped_winged plan as a stylised stand-in: the wings become the flight surface, the dangling hind limbs become the roost cling, beak_ratio is cut to 0.12 and coloured from the belly so the part reads as a short blunt muzzle rather than a beak, and the two large ears are extra parts on the head, sized and offset to stand clear of the skull rather than sit inside it. The poses are the plan's own built-in idle, fly, perched and rest cycles; perched is an upright cling, not an inverted hang, for the reason given under traits.perching. Proportions are authored around the sourced 39 cm wingspan and 7 cm head-and-body length.

behavior.note: Uses the shared fsm-ground-forager-v1 programme, which is written for a walking ground forager, with forage_gait and flee_gait set to fly so the bat flies between roost, water and feeding patches. The sun-based rest window is left at the programme's default (rest between 10 and 90 degrees of solar elevation), which puts the bat at its roost through the day and out foraging at night, matching its nocturnal pattern; flee_m is shortened to 12 m because a bat leaves a roost or an open porch well before a person is that close.
